text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today, rebounding after a volatile week that saw the stock down nearly 7% from late October highs. The bounce appears tied to a leadership change announced on October 29th, combined with a modest stabilization in crude oil prices (US oil holding at $103/barrel) and refinery utilization staying elevated at 92.8%, which supports the company's core refining margins. The stock had tumbled sharply on October 27th likely on investor caution around Big Oil earnings guidance, but today's recovery suggests some positive reception to the management shift and company update.

The broader backdrop remains mixed for refiners. While crude prices remain well above $100/barrel and refining capacity is running hard, the recent news cycle has turned skeptical on Big Oil's outsized profits—particularly as Trump's promised energy-cost cuts haven't materialized. This creates uncertainty about whether current high refining earnings will sustain, even as near-term supply tightness (gasoline and diesel inventories remain moderate) continues to support margins.
